output.title: Smooth Sliding Text Lines - Opposite Direction Typokinetics

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset where text lines slide past each other like film strips moving through a projector gate. Think of it as a continuous vertical conveyor belt where lines move upward on the left side and downward on the right side, creating a mesmerizing counter-motion effect. Each text line should have a subtle parallax effect where lines closer to the viewer move faster than those in the background. The animation should feel smooth and hypnotic, like watching credits roll in opposite directions. Use a staggered timing approach where each line starts its movement slightly offset from others, creating a wave-like initiation. Add a subtle fade-in and fade-out at the edges to simulate text entering and leaving the frame, similar to how objects disappear beyond the camera's field of view in traditional video editing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Use a BaseLayout container with 'relative overflow-hidden w-full h-full' classes. Create two vertical columns using 'flex flex-row gap-4'. Each column should be a BaseLayout with 'flex-1 relative'. For the sliding effect, use multiple TextAtom components wrapped in BaseLayout containers with 'absolute w-full' positioning. Apply translateY effects with AnimationRange from -100% to 100% for upward motion and 100% to -100% for downward motion. Use 'ease-linear' for continuous motion. Stagger each line's startOffset by 0.2s increments. Add opacity effects at 0-10% and 90-100% of each line's animation range for fade in/out. Set z-index using 'z-10', 'z-20', 'z-30' classes for depth layering. Use fitDurationTo: 'parent' for all text elements. Consider adding a subtle scale effect (0.9 to 1.1) for parallax depth.

prompts.prompt: Design a kinetic typography preset inspired by split-flap display boards at train stations. Text lines should slide horizontally in opposing directions with a mechanical, rhythmic quality. Imagine each line as a separate track where words slide in from opposite sides, pause briefly in the center for readability, then continue sliding out the other side. The motion should have a slight 'snap' quality at the pause points, mimicking the mechanical flip of split-flap displays. Layer multiple lines at different vertical positions, creating a grid-like composition. Add a subtle rotation on the Y-axis during the slide to simulate the 3D flip effect of physical boards. Include a brief 'hold' moment where all text aligns perfectly in the center before continuing their journey.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'grid grid-rows-3 gap-2 w-full h-full items-center' for vertical distribution. Each row contains a BaseLayout with 'relative h-full overflow-hidden'. TextAtom components use 'absolute whitespace-nowrap' positioning. Create a three-phase animation: slide-in (translateX from -150% to 0), hold (no transform for 20% of duration), slide-out (translateX from 0 to 150%). Use 'ease-in' for entry, 'ease-out' for exit. Add rotateY effect: 0deg to 15deg during slide-in, -15deg to 0deg during slide-out. Apply 'transform-style-preserve-3d perspective-1000' to parent containers. Alternate direction for odd rows using conditional logic. Use internal effect presets for the slide-hold-slide pattern. Set timing with relative values: 40% slide-in, 20% hold, 40% slide-out.

prompts.prompt: Create a liquid motion typokinetics effect where text lines flow past each other like streams of water. Think of it as typography caught in opposing currents - some text flows left-to-right while others flow right-to-left, with a fluid, organic motion. The text should have a wave-like undulation as it moves, similar to how text might appear when filmed underwater. Add a subtle distortion effect that makes the text appear to bend and flex as it passes through certain points, like light refracting through water. The crossing points where opposing text streams meet should create a brief 'turbulence' effect with slight scale and blur variations. This creates a dreamy, ethereal quality perfect for artistic or emotional content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full' containing multiple absolute-positioned layers. Use SVG filters for wave distortion by adding custom filter definitions. TextAtom components wrapped in BaseLayout with 'absolute w-full' and custom wave animation. Create sine wave motion using translateY combined with translateX: calculate Y position as Math.sin(progress * Math.PI * 4) * 20px. Apply CSS filter for blur: 0px to 2px at intersection points (50% progress). Use scale effect: 1 to 1.1 back to 1 at turbulence zones. Implement with generic effects using multiple AnimationRange entries for complex motion paths. Add 'will-change-transform' and 'transform-gpu' classes for performance. Use spring easing for organic feel. Consider adding a subtle hue-rotate filter animation for color shifting effect.

prompts.prompt: Build a carousel-style kinetic text preset where lines rotate around an invisible cylinder, creating a 3D revolving door effect. Visualize text lines as panels on a rotating display, where text on the front moves right while text on the back (visible through transparency) moves left. The rotation should create natural perspective changes - text grows larger as it approaches the viewer and shrinks as it recedes. Add depth of field simulation where distant text becomes slightly blurred and less opaque. The motion should be continuous and smooth, like a perfectly balanced rotating sculpture. Include subtle lighting effects where text brightens as it faces forward and dims as it rotates away.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full perspective-1000 transform-style-preserve-3d'. Create cylindrical rotation using rotateY transforms from 0deg to 360deg. Position TextAtom components at different rotation angles initially (0deg, 72deg, 144deg, 216deg, 288deg for 5 panels). Use translateZ(200px) to push text away from rotation center. Apply scale based on rotation angle: scale(1.2) at 0deg (front), scale(0.8) at 180deg (back). Implement opacity curve: 1 at front, 0.3 at back. Add blur filter: 0px at front, 3px at back. Use 'backface-visibility-hidden' for clean rotation. Create continuous rotation with linear easing over full duration. Consider using a sub-preset for individual rotating panels. Add 'transform-gpu' for hardware acceleration.

prompts.prompt: Design a glitch-inspired typokinetics preset where text lines slide past each other with digital interference patterns. Think of corrupted video data where text streams move in opposite directions but occasionally 'glitch' - briefly jumping position, duplicating, or distorting. The base motion should be smooth horizontal slides, but inject random micro-pauses and position shifts that simulate data corruption. Add RGB channel splitting during glitch moments where the text briefly separates into red, green, and blue components before snapping back together. Include scan line effects and brief static noise overlays at transition points. This creates an edgy, technological aesthetic perfect for modern, high-energy content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden'. Layer multiple TextAtom components with 'absolute mix-blend-screen'. Create base slide animation with translateX, interrupted by glitch frames. Use step() easing for glitch jumps: translateX with 'steps(3, jump-end)' for 0.1s intervals. RGB split: duplicate text 3 times with 'text-red-500', 'text-green-500', 'text-blue-500' classes and slight translateX offsets. Add random opacity flickers: keyframes alternating between 1 and 0.3. Create scan lines with ::before pseudo-element using 'bg-gradient-to-b from-transparent via-white/10 to-transparent'. Use internal effect presets for reusable glitch patterns. Implement glitch triggers at 25%, 50%, 75% of animation timeline. Add 'pointer-events-none' to prevent interaction issues.

prompts.prompt: Create a typewriter ribbon effect where text lines slide past each other like overlapping typewriter ribbons in motion. Each line should move with the mechanical precision of a typewriter carriage return - smooth horizontal motion with a slight 'bounce' at the end of each traverse. Layer the text with varying opacities to simulate the semi-transparent quality of ribbon ink. Add a subtle vertical offset that increases with each line, creating a cascading effect like paper feeding through a typewriter. Include character-by-character reveal as the text slides in, mimicking the sequential typing action. The crossing motion should feel rhythmic and purposeful, with brief pauses that echo the mechanical stops of vintage typewriters.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full font-mono' for typewriter aesthetic. Stack TextAtom components with increasing translateY offsets (0px, 20px, 40px, etc.) using 'absolute w-full'. Implement slide animation with bounce easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55)' for carriage return feel. Character reveal: use clip-path or width animation from 0 to 100% synchronized with horizontal slide. Apply opacity layers: 1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4 for ribbon overlap effect. Add slight rotateZ(-1deg to 1deg) for mechanical wobble. Create pause points at 0%, 45%, 55%, 100% of timeline for typewriter rhythm. Use 'tracking-wider' for authentic monospace appearance. Consider letter-spacing animation for carriage movement simulation. Include subtle text-shadow for ink bleed effect.

prompts.prompt: Develop a pendulum swing typokinetics where text lines swing past each other like synchronized pendulums. Imagine each line of text suspended from an invisible pivot point above the frame, swinging in opposing arcs. The motion should follow physics-accurate pendulum movement with natural acceleration at the bottom of the swing and deceleration at the peaks. Create a hypnotic pattern where odd lines swing left-to-right while even lines swing right-to-left. Add subtle rotation that follows the swing angle, making text tilt naturally with momentum. Include a gentle fade effect at the extreme points of the swing where text momentarily pauses before reversing direction. The overall effect should be meditative and rhythmic, like watching a Newton's cradle.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full flex flex-col justify-center'. Each TextAtom wrapped in BaseLayout with 'absolute w-full' and transform-origin set to 'top center' via style prop. Implement pendulum motion using rotateZ animation: -30deg to 30deg with sine-wave easing. Combine with translateX calculated from rotation angle: Math.sin(rotationRadians) * radius. Use 'cubic-bezier(0.445, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95)' for physics-accurate swing. Add subtle scaleY: 0.98 to 1.02 for momentum stretch. Apply opacity: 0.7 to 1 to 0.7 matching swing extremes. Create alternating patterns using index-based conditions. Set animation duration with slight variations (2s, 2.1s, 1.9s) for organic feel. Include 'transform-gpu' and 'will-change-transform' for smooth motion.

prompts.prompt: Build a marquee crossfade effect where text lines slide horizontally in opposite directions while continuously fading in and out. Think of it as multiple LED ticker displays layered on top of each other, each scrolling different content at varying speeds. The text should loop seamlessly, creating an infinite scroll effect. As lines cross paths, they should briefly intensify in brightness (like two lights overlapping) before continuing. Add a subtle glow effect that pulses with the movement, creating light trails behind moving text. The speed variation between lines creates visual depth - faster lines appear closer while slower lines recede into the background. This creates a dynamic, billboard-like aesthetic perfect for promotional or attention-grabbing content.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden'. Multiple TextAtom components with 'absolute whitespace-nowrap' positioned at different Y coordinates. Implement infinite scroll using translateX from 100% to -100% with 'animation-iteration-count-infinite'. Vary animation durations: 8s, 10s, 12s for speed depth. Add glow using text-shadow: '0 0 10px currentColor, 0 0 20px currentColor'. Create intensity boost at intersections using CSS variables and calc() for dynamic glow intensity. Use 'mix-blend-mode-screen' for light overlap effect. Add ::after pseudo-element with gradient mask for trail effect. Apply 'animation-timing-function-linear' for constant speed. Consider duplicating text content for seamless loop. Include 'text-stroke-1 text-stroke-white/20' for LED outline effect.

prompts.prompt: Create a film reel splice effect where text lines slide past each other like film strips being edited on a flatbed editor. Each line represents a different film strip moving through the editing bay - some forward, some reverse, with varying speeds that simulate scrubbing through footage. Add sprocket hole visualizations on the sides that move with the text, reinforcing the film strip metaphor. Include brief 'splice' moments where text appears to jump or skip frames, mimicking actual film cuts. The motion should have the mechanical precision of film transport with occasional organic imperfections. Add a subtle flicker effect reminiscent of projected film, with brightness variations that suggest the intermittent shutter of a projector.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gray-900 border-l-8 border-r-8 border-gray-800' for film edges. Add sprocket holes using repeating-linear-gradient in border styling. TextAtom components in BaseLayout wrappers with 'absolute w-full py-2'. Base motion: translateX with varying speeds (1x, 1.5x, 0.75x, -1x for reverse). Splice effect: use step() function at specific intervals - 'steps(1, jump-start)' for frame jumps. Add brightness flicker: animate opacity between 0.9-1.0 at 24fps intervals using CSS keyframes. Create film grain overlay with ::before using noise texture or CSS pattern. Implement occasional 'stuck frame' effect with animation-play-state toggle. Use 'font-mono uppercase' for technical film slate appearance. Add subtle sepia filter for vintage feel. Consider transform: scaleX(-1) for reverse playback visual cue.

prompts.prompt: Design a cosmic drift typokinetics where text lines float past each other like celestial bodies in space. Think of text as asteroids or space debris drifting through zero gravity - each line follows its own trajectory with subtle rotation and varying speeds. The motion should feel weightless and eternal, with text entering from various angles and floating across the viewport. Add a parallax star field effect where smaller, dimmer text elements move slower in the background while larger, brighter text moves faster in the foreground. Include a subtle gravitational influence where text lines slightly curve their paths when passing near each other. The overall effect should be serene and expansive, like watching objects drift through the cosmos.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden'. Create depth layers using z-index: multiple BaseLayout containers with 'absolute inset-0'. Foreground TextAtoms: 'text-white text-2xl opacity-100', midground: 'text-gray-300 text-lg opacity-70', background: 'text-gray-500 text-sm opacity-40'. Implement drift paths using combined transforms: translateX, translateY with bezier curves for non-linear motion. Add slow rotation: rotateZ from 0deg to 360deg over long duration (20-30s). Vary animation durations by layer: 10s (front), 20s (mid), 30s (back). Create gravitational curves using cubic-bezier paths when elements proximities detected. Add subtle glow: 'drop-shadow-[0_0_3px_rgba(255,255,255,0.5)]' for star-like quality. Use 'mix-blend-mode-add' for light interaction. Include random starting positions using CSS custom properties. Consider adding subtle scale pulsing for twinkling effect.
